before.paraphrase: Pārvatī asks why Nala performed the vow. Himavat describes Niṣadha’s king as Veda-knowing, brave, generous, wealthy and pure, skilled with chariot, sword, arrows, bow, quiver and armour, and able to travel the three worlds. before.details: After much time Budha visits sage Kalabha’s house while the sage bathes, seizes his beautiful wife by the hair, embraces, kisses and rapes her. Sulabhā says her parents’ given name has made her easy to him, condemns the assault in her husband’s absence and curses him to become a leper in another birth whose very name people will avoid. He flees frightened to the prostitute but resumes drink and pleasure. Brahmā declines further wrongdoings, saying telling others’ faults diminishes merit. Budha eventually dies; Yama orders messengers to throw him into hell until the elemental dissolution. Having endured that, he is born in a Vaiśya home, severely leprous through the sage’s wife’s curse. The discourse condemns his deeds, prescribes clothed bathing after touching him and avoidance of his name, and says removing him will raise the craft.
